headline_marked: 13-year-old boy [[killed for an iPhone]], body found in Cumilla jungle
headline: 13-year-old boy killed for an iPhone, body found in Cumilla jungle
summary: Ishiat Shahriar Opratim disappeared after leaving home to meet friends; police suspect the theft of his mother's phone was the motive for the murder.
details: Ishiat Shahriar Opratim, a 13-year-old student of Comilla Border Guard Public School, was found dead in a jungle at Lalmai Pahar in Cumilla.
The boy had left home around 3:00 pm the previous day to meet friends, carrying his mother's iPhone. His body was discovered the following afternoon with injury marks on his head.
Police and university teachers preliminarily suspect that the iPhone was the motive for the killing, as the device has not yet been recovered.
Opratim was the only son of Nahida Begum, an associate professor at Comilla University, and businessman KM Firoz Shahriar.
The family had filed a general diary and appealed on social media for help before the body was located through CCTV footage review.
According to Ain o Salish Kendra, 254 child deaths were recorded across Bangladesh between January and August this year, with 110 children aged 13 to 18.
Police are continuing their investigation to identify those responsible and establish the exact motive behind the crime.
caption:
A 13-year-old boy's life may have been taken for a smartphone. His body was found in a Cumilla jungle with head injuries.

Ishiat Shahriar Opratim, a 13-year-old student of Comilla Border Guard Public School, was found dead in a jungle at Lalmai Pahar in Cumilla.

The boy had left home around 3:00 pm the previous day to meet friends, carrying his mother's iPhone. His body was discovered the following afternoon with injury marks on his head.

Police and university teachers preliminarily suspect that the iPhone was the motive for the killing, as the device has not yet been recovered.

Opratim was the only son of Nahida Begum, an associate professor at Comilla University, and businessman KM Firoz Shahriar.

The family had filed a general diary and appealed on social media for help before the body was located through CCTV footage review.

According to Ain o Salish Kendra, 254 child deaths were recorded across Bangladesh between January and August this year, with 110 children aged 13 to 18.

Police are continuing their investigation to identify those responsible and establish the exact motive behind the crime.

headline_marked: [[Three buses set ablaze]] in Dhaka; crude bomb blasts rock city
headline: Three buses set ablaze in Dhaka; crude bomb blasts rock city
summary: Multiple buses were targeted in arson attacks across Dhaka, while crude bombs exploded in several locations, prompting increased security measures across the capital.
details: A passenger bus belonging to Shikhor Paribahan was set on fire in Mirpur-11, Dhaka, on Saturday evening. The fire service was alerted at 7:13 PM and two units were dispatched to the scene. The blaze, which occurred while the bus was in motion, was extinguished, and preliminary investigations suggest a mechanical fault as the cause. No casualties were reported.

Simultaneously, another bus from Obhijatri Paribahan was targeted near the Ansar Camp in Mirpur-1. Local residents assisted in extinguishing the fire before it could spread significantly. The Officer-in-Charge of Mirpur Police Station confirmed no injuries.

Later, at around 8 PM, a bus belonging to Alif Paribahan, parked by the roadside in Modhyo Badda, was also set on fire. Suspects reportedly ignited the rear of the bus before fleeing the scene. The fire was put out by bystanders.

These incidents follow a series of crude bomb explosions that occurred on Friday. Explosions were reported in Malibagh, Agargaon, Mohakhali, Babubazar Bridge, Mogbazar, and Jatrabari. One auto-rickshaw driver, Ibadur Rahman, was injured in the Jatrabari explosions.

Authorities have registered cases related to these incidents, but the perpetrators remain unidentified. In response to the escalating violence, the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) has heightened security across the capital. Checkpoints have been established at key locations, and police patrols and surveillance have been intensified.
